topic.title: Learned Shape Representations and Editable Surface Geometry
topic.overview: Three-dimensional shape learning must choose how geometry is stored and manipulated. Implicit fields, explicit meshes, learned surface elements, and hybrid tetrahedral representations make different tradeoffs in topology, detail, correspondence, and editability. The represented methods increasingly connect these forms through differentiable reconstruction and optimization.
topic.whyItMatters: A representation suitable for rendering may be awkward for physical editing or temporal consistency. Maintaining a usable surface structure matters when generated assets must be animated, matched across objects, or incorporated into downstream design tools.
topic.evolution: Early examples learn view transitions and qualitative shape from motion. The 2019–2021 papers develop reusable surface structures, differentiable mesh extraction, and hybrid representations. Recent representatives add dynamic text-guided meshes, uncertainty-aware anatomical shapes, and executable CAD generation. This expands the kinds of control sought from a shape model rather than proving one representation best for every task.
openQuestions: How can generated geometry remain editable while allowing topology changes?
What constraints preserve identity and surface consistency through animation?
